title: Delay: echoes
learned: An insert effect goes into the chain of one sound: out of the voice, into the effect, on to the console
TIME is the gap between the echoes, FEEDBACK how many come back
MIX sets dry (the original) against wet (the effect)

steps.why: An effect changes a sound that already exists. The simplest way to use one is as an insert: put it in the chain of a single sound, between the voice and the console.
steps.do: A sparse melody plays into channel 1 of the console. A delay (JX-DLY) is in the rack. Press Next.

steps.why: The sound goes out of the amplifier, into the delay, and from the delay to the console.
steps.do: Hold Ctrl and drag a new cable from OUT 1 of the amplifier to IN of the delay. Then drag OUT of the delay to IN 1 of the console (it replaces the amplifier's cable there).
steps.after: Every note now comes back as a row of fading echoes. The delay records the sound and plays it again a moment later, and feeds part of the repeat back in, so it repeats again.

steps.why: TIME is the gap between the echoes.
steps.do: Press F1 and turn TIME of the delay.
steps.after: Short times (under 50 ms) thicken the sound or make it ring metallic; a few hundred milliseconds give clear echoes. Echoes that land on the beat sound musical: at 110 BPM an eighth note is about 270 ms. Turning TIME while notes ring bends their pitch, like tape.

steps.why: FEEDBACK is how much of each echo goes back in.
steps.do: Turn FEEDBACK up, then down again.
steps.after: Low feedback: one or two echoes. High: a long trail. Near the top the echoes keep building into a warm drone; the delay holds them back softly so they never blow up.

steps.why: MIX sets the original (dry) against the echoes (wet).
steps.after: Left: only the original. Right: only the echoes. In between: both. An insert effect usually sits somewhere in the middle.
steps.try: Turn TONE: left makes every repeat darker (like an old tape echo), right thinner.

steps.do: Voice → effect → console: an insert changes one sound. Press Next to finish.
